title: lead-n69n: R6 sonnet->haiku per-node model fallback NOT expressible in fabro 0.254.0 (blocked); R7 fabro engage exec not detached (fixable)
description:
Refs lead-n69n (request_bugfix, scenarios:[]).

R6 (BLOCKING — structurally impossible in fabro 0.254.0):
The lead asked for a per-node/per-class sonnet-4-5 -> haiku-4-5 model FALLBACK CHAIN on all .coding/.review nodes, authored in the workflow.fabro model_stylesheet (lead believed the stylesheet supports fallbacks:). EMPIRICAL FINDING against the real cached fabro 0.254.0 (/tmp/fabro-cache/fabro validate --no-upgrade-check --json):
  * The stylesheet parser (lib/crates/fabro-graphviz/src/stylesheet.rs) silently ACCEPTS arbitrary unknown properties: a rule '.coding { model: claude-sonnet-4-5; zzzznonsense: whatever }' validates clean (valid=true, 0 diagnostics beyond the benign inputs.BC_NAME template warning).
  * A BOGUS PRIMARY model IS caught: stylesheet 'model:' -> stylesheet_model_known; node 'model=' -> node_model_known. But a BOGUS FALLBACK model (stylesheet 'fallbacks:[claude-bogus-9-9]' OR node 'fallbacks="claude-bogus-9-9"') is NOT caught -> proof 'fallbacks' is swallowed/ignored, not parsed into the model spec.
  * The known NODE-attribute enumeration in the binary is: acp_command, model, shape, backend, timeout, goal_gate, selection, deterministic, stall_timeout, default_thread — 'fallbacks' is NOT among them.
  * The 'fallbacks' field (ModelRef: required [provider,name,fallbacks]) is an API/registry schema field: 'Alternative names that resolve to this model. example: ["opus"]' — model-registry aliases configured at install/registry time, NOT a per-node runtime fallback chain authorable in a .fabro.
CONCLUSION: writing fallbacks: into the stylesheet is a FALSE-GREEN — it passes fabro validate + the R6 structural test but fabro DISCARDS it; the .coding/.review nodes stay sonnet-only at runtime and STILL fail-close on the persistent sonnet-429. The only DSL-honored options both violate an explicit lead constraint: (a) change .coding/.review stylesheet model: to haiku = PERMANENT DOWNGRADE (lead forbade); (b) graph-structural twin-haiku fallback nodes on failure edges = CHANGES node/edge counts + graph shape (lead said counts unchanged; would require re-pinning scn 75 2dfefe2ba81e418d). Needs lead direction.

R7 (root cause CONFIRMED, cleanly fixable): controller.py:2971 _fabro_engage issues the engage via self._driver.exec_run(...) WITHOUT detach — a synchronous docker exec whose internally-backgrounded { nohup server & } { nohup run & } children inherit the exec's stdout/stderr pipes, so exec_run never sees EOF and launch() blocks. Fix per lead: mirror the tmux path (controller.py:3073 tmux new-session -d) — either add a detach=True (docker exec -d) capability to the driver exec_run, or wrap the engage in tmux new-session -d. NOT applied because R6 blocks the dispatch as a whole (acceptance requires R6+R7+release).

Real-fabro verified: baseline committed workflow.fabro validate = valid:true, 23 nodes, 45 edges, 1 benign template warning.

notes:
Lead work_id: lead-vzxd.5
mechanism_observation: Clarify.work_id pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$ rejects dotted sub-bead work_ids the lead actually dispatches (e.g. lead-vzxd.5) — ## What was observed

The lead dispatched this maintenance under work_id `lead-vzxd.5` (a dotted sub-bead id under epic `lead-vzxd`). `shop-msg pending inbox` and `read inbox` both surface it verbatim as `lead-vzxd.5`. But `shop-msg respond clarify --work-id lead-vzxd.5` raises a pydantic ValidationError: `Clarify.work_id` carries `pattern='^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'` (MinLen 1), which forbids the `.` separator. So the BC **cannot emit a clarify that echoes back the very work_id the inbox delivered**.

## Why it is load-bearing (not scope of this work item)

1. **Asymmetry across the response schemas.** `WorkDone.work_id` has NO pattern constraint (empty metadata) and accepts `lead-vzxd.5` fine; `MechanismObservation.work_id` likewise. Only `Clarify.work_id` carries the dot-forbidding regex. A BC that needs to CLARIFY a dotted-work_id dispatch is silently forced to route through `work_done --status blocked` instead — which is exactly what happened here: this dispatch's substantive outcome is a clarify (a spec contradiction needing lead judgment), but it had to ride the blocked channel because clarify was unemittable.

2. **The system elsewhere EXPECTS dotted lead-bead ids.** The pinned scenarios v0.3.0 validator's @origin prefix rule (`_LEAD_BEAD_SUFFIX_RE = ^[a-z0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$`) EXPLICITLY accepts dotted lead-bead ids like `lead-vzxd.1` as legal @origin values. So dotted sub-bead ids are a first-class, sanctioned identifier shape in one part of the system while `Clarify` forbids them in another — an internal inconsistency, not a caller error.

3. **Reconciliation risk.** Routing a clarify-shaped outcome through `work_done(blocked)` changes the lead's expected message_type for the dispatch. A lead awaiting a `clarify` on a dotted work_id may not reconcile a `work_done(blocked)` the same way, and the BC has no clean channel to ask its question.

## Proposed action

Relax `Clarify.work_id` (and audit `WorkDone`/`MechanismObservation` for consistency) to accept the dotted sub-bead suffix — e.g. align on the scenarios validator's `^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+(\.[0-9]+)*$` shape — so a clarify can echo the exact dispatched work_id. Until then, BCs receiving dotted work_ids cannot emit clarify and must fall back to `work_done(blocked)`.

mechanism_observation: shop-msg has no first-class BC-side blocked-retriable / re-queue primitive; F2 had to use the nudge side-channel — ## Observation (load-bearing messaging-mechanism gap)

While landing F2 of lead-i0wi (a fail-closed fabro run must not permanently consume/lose the inbox dispatch), we hit a structural gap in the shop-msg messaging mechanism itself — not a property of this work item.

**shop-msg has NO first-class BC-side re-queue / blocked-retriable primitive.** Once ANY outbox response is emitted for a work_id, the dispatch is permanently de-pended:

- 'shop-msg send' REFUSES to overwrite an existing inbox message (no re-deposit path from the BC side).
- 'shop-msg consume outbox' does NOT re-pend the originating inbox dispatch.
- 'respond work_done --status blocked' terminates the dispatch just like complete — the pending row is gone, so a blocked run is NOT retriable without the lead re-dispatching.

**Consequence / current workaround.** To satisfy F2's requirement that a fail-closed run stay *retriable without lead re-dispatch*, emit_blk had to report the blocked state via the NON-CONSUMING 'shop-msg nudge' side-channel rather than through a proper work_done/blocked response — deliberately leaving the dispatch pending so a re-run can pick it up. This works, but it is a side-channel workaround: the 'blocked-but-retriable' semantic is not expressible as a first-class outbox response.

**Why this warrants a mechanism_observation (not a clarify/blocked).** This is a property of the messaging mechanism/schema — the absence of a re-arm primitive — that any BC running a fail-closed orchestrator (fabro or otherwise) will hit, not a property of the lead-i0wi work item. It is load-bearing because the nudge workaround is fragile: it depends on emit_blk correctly NOT consuming, and a future refactor could silently reintroduce consume-and-lose.

The shop-msg OUTBOX is keyed by (work_id, message_type), so multiple message types CAN coexist under one work_id — e.g. a work_done AND a mechanism_observation on the same lead work_id live as separate rows. BUT 'shop-msg read outbox --work-id <id>' surfaces only the SINGLE most-recent row (no message-type selector), so after you emit a mechanism_observation on a work_id that already has a work_done, read-outbox shows ONLY the observation and a naive grep reports '0 work_done' — a DISPLAY limitation, NOT data loss. To see all rows use 'shop-msg dump --direction outbox'. The CLI has an idempotency guard: 'respond work_done' refuses to overwrite an existing work_done ('use --force to replace') — do NOT --force to 'restore' a work_done that read-outbox seems to be missing; --force would REPLACE the genuine original with a reconstructed copy. Always premise-check with 'dump' before any --force. (Filed mechanism_observation jje + this memory after a near-miss this session.) Practical guidance: when emitting a mechanism_observation, keying it to the lead work_id is fine (coexists with work_done), but using a distinct BC-side --work-id + --observed-during <lead-id> avoids the read-outbox display confusion entirely.
